jobs.title: Automation Engineer - Facilities SCADA & PLC (f/m/d)
jobs.description: The Role We are looking for an experienced Automation Engineer to take technical ownership of the Facilities Monitoring and Control System (FMCS) that keeps our fab running - the system that supervises every utility our production depends on, from cleanroom air and chilled water to process cooling, exhaust and power monitoring. The system is delivered and commissioned by an external integrator; from handover, it's yours. You won't be building it from scratch - you'll be the person who understands it well enough to keep it running, diagnose it when it misbehaves, extend it as we grow from pilot line to full production, and hold suppliers to account. If the FMCS has an issue at 03:00, you're the one who knows what to do. To join our team, you should be excited to: Operate, monitor and maintain our SCADA system (Siemens WinCC OA or Yokogawa DCS Centum) across servers, operator stations and displays Maintain and diagnose our Siemens S7-1500 PLCs and their remote I/O, and adapt control logic within the existing standardised structure Plan and perform loop checks end to end - tracing each signal from the field device through wiring, I/O and PLC all the way to the operator screen, and confirming that commands actually move valves, dampers and actuators Investigate and resolve alarms, communication faults and unexpected equipment behaviourduring live operation Verify instrument calibration and troubleshoot analog and digital field signals - multimeter in hand, not only from a screen Add new datapoints, screens, trends and reports, and tune alarms so operators trust the system Keep documentation current - as-built drawings, tag lists, change records - and uphold change control Act as the technical counterpart to contractors and vendors, and support qualification and audits with system evidence Your Qualifications One of two equivalent qualification paths: a completed apprenticeship as an Electronics Technician for Automation Technology plus further training as a state-certified technician (Techniker), or comparable - or a degree in Electrical Engineering, Automation Engineering or a related field, or comparable 5+ years of hands-on experience with industrial SCADA and PLC systems in a production environment - commissioning, operating or supporting, not only design Solid experience with Siemens S7 PLCs (TIA Portal / Step 7) - going online, reading and modifying logic, diagnosing faults on a running plant; experience with comparable PLC platforms is also welcome Strong SCADA engineering skills - ideally Siemens WinCC OA or Yokogawa DCS Centum, but experience with another platform (e.g. WinCC, PCS 7, Ignition, Aveva, Zenon) plus the willingness to grow into WinCC OA is just as welcome Practical experience with loop checks, instrument calibration and signal troubleshooting, and with reading P&IDs, loop diagrams and I/O lists A structured, disciplined approach to documentation and change control, and the confidence to say no to a change that compromises safety

jobs.title: Supplier Quality Engineer
jobs.description: ANYbotics is a fast-growing tech company dedicated to shaping the future of mobile robotics across multiple industries. Join our highly talented and motivated team of more than 200 people and work on cutting-edge robot technology. The Opportunity As a Supplier Quality Engineer, you will own supplier quality for a portfolio of critical mechanical, electrical and mechatronic suppliers, from supplier qualification through production and continuous improvement. The role exists to strengthen our supplier quality processes as ANYbotics scales production and introduces new products. You will work closely with Procurement, Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, and will spend time directly with suppliers to solve quality issues at the source. This is a hands-on role: you will not only define processes and requirements, but also audit suppliers, drive corrective actions and make sure improvements are implemented and sustained. Your Impact Your Impact Define supplier qualification criteria and establish robust processes for assessing and approving new suppliers. Prepare and maintain supplier audit and assessment frameworks, including questionnaires and checklists. Conduct on-site assessments of critical suppliers and drive audit findings through to closure. Monitor supplier performance, identify recurring quality issues and initiate improvement or development actions where needed. Identify suppliers, manufacturers and service providers requiring Quality Assurance Agreements (QAAs). Develop and maintain QAA templates aligned with ISO 9001 and ISO 80079-34 requirements. Review and negotiate QAA terms with suppliers, covering responsibilities, control points, traceability, non-conformities and other quality requirements. Coordinate internal Quality, Legal and Purchasing approvals for QAAs and monitor ongoing supplier compliance. Define and maintain the supplier NCR process, from detection and reporting through escalation, follow-up and closure. Establish effective NCR templates and tracking tools, and communicate non-conformities clearly with suppliers. Analyse NCR trends and recurring issues to identify systemic quality problems and drive corrective actions. Initiate supplier development, improvement plans or requalification where supplier performance falls below expectations. Your Profile 5 years  experience in supplier quality management with complex mechatronic product Hands-on experience conducting supplier audits and driving corrective actions through to verified closure. Strong understanding of root-cause analysis, 8D  and structured problem solving. Experience defining and negotiating supplier quality requirements, ideally including Quality Assurance Agreements. Ability to work effectively across Procurement, Engineering, Manufacturing and Quality, while challenging suppliers when quality or delivery requirements are not met. Willingness to travel to suppliers and spend time on-site when required. Bonus Points Experience with ISO 9001 and/or ISO 8007

jobs.title: Engineering Manager - EU
jobs.description: Hi 👋 I’m Colin , Director of Engineering, Europe. How do you feel about software engineers writing product specs, making product decisions, and not breaking down projects into individual tickets? If that sounds exciting (even if a bit scary), read on because I’m looking for an engineering manager to help us build a different type of engineering team and culture at Ashby. To start, why do we need to be different? Time and again, I have witnessed engineers knowing what needs to be done yet being unable to get things done because of “the process” or because “more data is needed.” Some of the most effective projects have been skunkworks projects, where engineers have taken total ownership of a problem and driven it to completion. I want to normalize that at Ashby. When we think about how these processes came about, we realize they carry a pessimistic mindset. They box people into smaller roles to minimize the chance of not meeting a certain standard. At Ashby. we’re building an environment that is optimistic about what engineers can own and achieve and embraces the innovative engineers (and frankly, often stays out of their way). To accomplish this, our engineering leaders need to think deeply about individual performance, process, and culture - not running sprint planning or driving product and technical decisions. You’ll focus on building your team, their skills to thrive with the ownership they’re given, and an environment that empowers them to do their best work consistently, with little distraction. For junior EMs we try to stay within 6 direct reports. This enables them to spend time with our teams observing, correcting, praising, and, yes, coding. We like our managers to be hands-on while also making sure they’re not on the critical path. We’ve already gathered an experienced, talented, and collaborative team of 25+ engineers. You’ll help me manage the growing team of engineers in Europe. In addition to working with engineers you’ll also get to work on projects yourselves. Some examples of work our engineering leaders have done: Provide feedback on product and technical specs to help engineers identify where to cut scope or improve quality. You don’t make the final decisions, but you’ll influence and coach ICs to reach the right ones. Grow engineers to the point where they can take large, loosely defined projects, and deliver them with little intervention. They still ask for help when needed - the difference is that they’re driving. Jump into our systems and code to debug a customer issue, ship a small bug fix, or improve our developer experience. Engineering leaders at Ashby are great engineers and enjoy keeping their skills up-to-date (while staying off the critical path). Improve how we generate and simulate data in demo accounts. It’s a project off the critical path, but it helps you keep up-to-date on our codebase while immensely impacting the business, from Engineering to QA to Sales. Why be a manager? Customer support has been the same job for twenty years: a queue, a ticket, an SLA, a closed case. That's ending, fast. Over the next 6–9 months, AI will take on more of the routine, repetitive cases at Elation. That doesn't shrink the human role — it builds on it. Significant professional or research experience in hardware engineering, product development, systems integration, testing, validation, reliability, or failure analysis. Demonstrated ownership of a substantial engineering problem—for example, a product or subsystem that reached production, a model validated against physical testing, a test system you developed, or a difficult failure you diagnosed. Experience working with Coding Agents is a must Process: Apply to the role and complete the screening questions. Complete an AI interview of approximately 30 minutes.
